content.summary_of_the_paper: The major contribution of the paper is the pseudo tokens to serve as a feature bank that stores the most representative images/text. The pseudo token is then used as a unifier for medical text and image pre-training. The paper is strong in the experiments, on a list of tasks on uni-modal, cross-modal, and multi-modal on three large datasets with both images and text.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

The most important contribution of the paper is the pseudo token, which will make Med-VLP model compatible with different kinds of inputs.

The experiments tend to be complete and cover a variety of tasks. 

Weaknesses:

The pseudo token introduced in the paper seems effective. Most of the other components, such as the MLM, ITM, and ITC are not new in the vision and language pre-training. The limitation of the pseudo token is not well discussed. What are the extra computational and memory cost of the pseudo token?

The experiments are thorough and complete on a list of image and text tasks. However, in Table 1, it is not clear what are the SOTA methods in the previous work. It is also not clear if those are still the SOTA so far in the literature. For example, on CheXpert leaderboard, more than 100 groups have achieved AUC higher than 90.1.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is clear to understand. The novelty lies in that the proposed model is able to be compatible with different kinds of inputs. 
The method seems reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper is well written in general. However, the effectiveness of the proposed method is not well supported by the experiments.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper considers both computer vision and natural language processing with medical data. Most importantly, it contributes to multi-modal data science and analytics by introducing and illustrating how a single model alone is able to process image-only, text-only, and paired-image-text data.
content.strength_and_weaknesses: The paper is clearly written and motivated. Namely, it excels in communicating a fundamental problem in machine/deep learning approaches (i.e., current limitations of siloed methods for computer vision and natural language processing), using this strong discipline foundation to motivate a practical problem in processing medical data where often both image and text modalities are present, and introduce and evaluate a model to address this limitation. Unfortunately, however, the paper does not devote sufficient space to describe and justify its experiments, although the evaluation results seem to be good and include, for instance, an ablation study to further elaborate on what makes the model successful. For example, it does not address human research ethics of using three datasets with data from human participants for the purposes of this study - although the data have been previously released, addressing ethics by, for example, obtaining a low risk ethics approval, addressing how datasets were created ethically (noting that no new data were collected as part of this particular study), and considering ethics and impacts of this study more broadly would be an important extension of the paper. To continue, statistical testing of the evaluation results (e.g., effect sizes, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests) seems to be lacking or insufficiently reported in the paper. Finally, the paper would benefit from revisions to communicate its key message more clearly by, for example, assuring that each paragraph has a topic sentence, and paying more careful attention to tense (e.g., past tense should be used for materials, methods, and experiments were chosen, justified, completed, and interpreted to differentiate the study from work on progress).

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a unified architecture to implement both Dual Encoder and Fusion Encoder for medical vision-and-language pre-training (MedVLP). Specifically, the Fusion Encoder is employed as the common backbone. To support ITC which requires single-modal training data, authors incorporate pseudo tokens from the other modal for compatibility. The method uses a pool for selecting the closest cross-modal pseudo token. The entire architecture is pre-trained with MLM, ITM and ITC. Experiments on three benchmarks are conducted, and the proposed architecture outperforms SOTA results. Analyses show the contributions w.r.t. each component and the suggestion of the pool size.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
    1. This paper studies an important task of MedVLP, which is of great interest for both academic and industrial community. 
    2. The proposed unified architecture for MedVLP integrates merits from both the dual-encoder paradigm and the fusion-encoder paradigm. 
    3. The design is empirically verified by extensive experiments on three benchmarks and ablation studies. 

Weaknesses
    1. Technical contributions are not very significant, since the unifying seems straightforward. As a key component to achieve unification, the design of Pseudo Tokens generally follows existing work. 
    2. In terms of Pseudo Tokens, a notable difference from existing work is that, the pseudo tokens are selected from a pool according to similarity score. However, it’s not clear why such a strategy is superior to using static or constant pseudo tokens. 
    3. Some important parts are confusing in experiments. (1) In Table 1, what are SOTA1 and SOTA2? I think it’s better to use specific algorithm names or literature citations. Furthermore, are all experiments conducted on the same setting (e.g. strategies for pre-processing, training budgets and so on)? (2) Some results in Table 2 seem inconsistent with Table 1. To my understanding, ID-3(only using MLM and ITM) is an existing Fusion Encoder architecture, so it’s among the SOTA methods. However, SOTA1/2 results in Table 1 are generally lower than ID3 in Table 2, e.g. CheXpert: ID3-88.4/SOTA2-88.1, MIMIC BL-4: ID3-9.9/SOTA2-8.2, VQA-RAD: ID3-77.7/SOTA1-72.7 …
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is generally clear and of a good quality. Novelty seems limited. Reproducibility is poor since codes are not provided.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper presents promising experimental results (if reliable) on MedVLP by unifying the Fusion and Dual paradigms. Technical novelty is not very strong. Concerns about Pseudo Token Selection and experimental results should be addressed to improve the paper.

content.title: PTUnifier: Pseudo Tokens as Paradigm Unifiers in Medical Vision-and-Language Pre-training
content.TL;DR: This paper proposes a simple approach to extract generic representations from medical images and texts, which can be applied to a broad range of medical tasks.
content.abstract: Medical vision-and-language pre-training (Med-VLP) has shown promising improvements on many downstream medical tasks owing to its applicability to extracting generic representations from medical images and texts. Practically, there exist two typical paradigms, i.e., the \textbf{fusion-encoder paradigm} and the \textbf{dual-encoder paradigm}, depending on whether a heavy fusion module is used. The former outperforms on multi-modal tasks owing to the sufficient interaction between modalities; the latter outperforms on uni-modal and cross-modal tasks due to the single-modality encoding ability. To take advantage of these two paradigms, we propose an effective yet straightforward scheme named PTUnifier to unify the two paradigms thanks to the identical input format by introducing visual and textual pseudo tokens, which serve as a feature bank that stores the most representative images/texts. By doing so, a single model could process various tasks adopting different input formats (i.e., image-only, text-only, and image-text-pair). Furthermore, we construct a pool of pseudo tokens (instead of static ones) to improve diversity and scalability. Experimental results show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on a broad range of tasks, spanning uni-modal tasks (i.e., image/text classification and text summarization), cross-modal tasks (i.e., image-to-text generation and image-text/text-image retrieval), and multi-modal tasks (i.e., visual question answering), demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach. Note that the adoption of pseudo tokens is orthogonal to most existing Med-VLP approaches, and we believe that our approach could be a beneficial and complementary extension to these approaches.
